# dpbrfs

> Improves the computed solution to a system `A * X = B` where `A` is symmetric positive definite band, and provides error bounds.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dpbrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dpbrfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dpbrfs(
    order,
    uplo,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, LDAB,
    AFB, LDAFB,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether 'upper' or 'lower' triangle is stored |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of superdiagonals (or subdiagonals) of A<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Original symmetric band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of AB<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `AFB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Cholesky-factored band matrix (from dpbtrf) |
| ↳ `LDAFB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of AFB<br>Column-major requires `LDAFB ≥ kd + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAFB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Right-hand side matrix (column-major) |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of B<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `X` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Solution matrix (improved on exit) |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of X<br>Column-major requires `LDX ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDX ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Output forward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Output backward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 3\*N) |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace array (length >= N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.
- `AFB`: The triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$ of the band matrix A as computed by DPBTRF, in the same storage format as A (see `AB`).
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DPBTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dpbrfs.strided(
    uplo,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    AFB, strideAFB1, strideAFB2, offsetAFB,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Improves the computed solution to a real system A * X = B where A is symmetric positive definite band and provides error bounds.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'lower'`, `'upper'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `uplo === 'upper'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `uplo === 'lower'`.<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X.<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` |
| `AFB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideAFB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AFB` |
| ↳ `strideAFB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AFB` |
| ↳ `offsetAFB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AFB` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `X` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `FERR` |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `BERR` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.
- `AFB`: The triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$ of the band matrix A as computed by DPBTRF, in the same storage format as A (see `AB`).
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DPBTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dpbtrf from './../../dpbtrf/lib/base.js';
import dpbtrs from './../../dpbtrs/lib/base.js';
import dpbrfs from './../lib/base.js';

// 3x3 SPD band matrix with KD=1, upper band storage (LDAB=2):

// Full: [4 1 0; 1 5 1; 0 1 6]
const ab = new Float64Array( [ 0.0, 4.0, 1.0, 5.0, 1.0, 6.0 ] );
const afb = new Float64Array( ab );

// Factorize
dpbtrf( 'upper', 3, 1, afb, 1, 2, 0 );

// Right-hand side
const b = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );

// Solve
const x = new Float64Array( b );
dpbtrs( 'upper', 3, 1, 1, afb, 1, 2, 0, x, 1, 3, 0 );

// Refine solution
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 9 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 3 );

const info = dpbrfs( 'upper', 3, 1, 1, ab, 1, 2, 0, afb, 1, 2, 0, b, 1, 3, 0, x, 1, 3, 0, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'x:', x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DPBRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DPBRFS improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations when the coefficient matrix is symmetric positive definite and banded, and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

</section>
